title: Castle early
summary: Castle by move 8. A king in the middle is a target. Develop first, then castle short in most games.
body:
### Castle early

Castling does two jobs. It moves your king to safety. It also brings a rook into the game.

At your level, a king in the middle is a big target. Your opponent opens the e-file or the d-file and attacks the king with checks. You can then lose a piece or the game. A castled king hides behind its pawns.

Use this plan:

- Develop your knights and bishops first.
- Clear the squares between your king and your rook.
- Castle by move 8 if you can. Castling short (O-O) is quicker and safer for most players.
- Then connect your rooks and fight for the centre.

Check these points before you castle:

- Your king is not in check.
- Your king does not cross or land on a square that your opponent attacks.
- You have not moved your king or that rook before.

After you castle, keep the pawns in front of your king at home. They are your shield. A pawn move like g4 early in the game makes holes near your king. A move like f4 opens a diagonal to your king.

Sometimes you cannot castle yet. A piece blocks the way, or an enemy piece attacks a square on the path. Solve that problem first. Do not waste time with a move like Ke2 when you can still castle.

A king can stay in the centre for a while when the centre is closed. Pawns then block the files. If your opponent opens the centre, castle at once.

Rule of thumb: develop your knights and bishops, then castle. A king in the centre is a target.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Make your king safe.
exercises.explanation: O-O puts the king behind its pawns and brings the rook towards the centre. You have a knight and a bishop out, so there is no reason to wait.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. Make your king safe.
exercises.explanation: The bishop left f8 and the g8 knight is gone, so the squares between king and rook are empty. O-O keeps the king safe when the centre opens and brings the rook to f8.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Make your king safe.
exercises.explanation: The bishop on b4 pins the knight on c3 to your king. O-O removes the pin and puts the king in a safe place.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Make your king safe.
exercises.explanation: The knight and the bishop are out, and f1 and g1 are empty. O-O is the natural next step. Waiting leaves the king on e1 for no reason.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. Make your king safe.
exercises.explanation: Black has two knights and a bishop out, so the king can go to safety. O-O gets the king out of the centre before White opens the position.
